Date: 8/5/26

## GOHREP

**Goal:**

Conduct exploratory data analysis of the cell death area score dataset by visualising scoring patterns with ggplot2 in R.

---

## 1. Setup

### 1.1 Load required packages

```{r}
#| output: false
# 1.1
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(here)
library(patchwork)
library(png)
library(tiff)
```

### 1.2 Load data

Data loaded from the output of `01_generate_raw_data/04_median_and_centre_coords`. Rater IDs are already anonymised (1–10).

```{r}
# 1.2
path_data <- here("analyses", "01_generate_raw_data", "04_median_and_centre_coords", "combined_cda_data_median.csv")

raw_data <- read_csv(path_data, show_col_types = FALSE)

score_data <- raw_data %>%
  select(Basename, Row, Col, Pos, Scorer1, Score1, Scorer2, Score2, Scorer3, Score3, Median_Score) %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(Scorer1, Scorer2, Scorer3), as.character),
    across(c(Score1, Score2, Score3), as.character)
  )

score_data_no0 <- score_data %>%
  filter(Median_Score != 0)

head(score_data)
```

There are 6,364 rows.

### 1.3 Helper functions and colour palettes

```{r}
# 1.3.1
source(here("src", "data_helpers.R"))
source(here("src", "plotting_helpers.R"))

save_plot <- make_save_plot("02_score_distributions")
```

```{r}
# 1.3.2
score_data_long <- long_score_table(score_data, drop_missing_scores = FALSE)

score_data_valid <- score_data_long %>%
  filter(!grepl("\\[\\]", Score), !is.na(Score)) %>%
  mutate(Score = as.integer(Score))
```

---

## 2. Raw scores

### 2.1 Example CDAs and scoring key

```{r}
# 2.1
# Scoring key (scores 0-6, left to right). The original key is a CMYK JPEG, so an
# sRGB copy (converted via its ICC profile) is read here to keep colours faithful.
# The number strip is cropped off (rows 189-554 keep just the 7 panels). The example
# columns carry the score labels and are boxed to the same width as the key panels.
key <- readPNG(here("analyses", "02_score_distributions", "assets", "lesion_score_key_rgb.png"))
key_raster <- as.raster(key[189:554, , 1:3])
W <- dim(key)[2] # key width (px)
key_h <- length(189:554) # cropped key height (panels only)

# key panel edges (measured) -> example column boxes match these exactly
L <- c(7, 404, 801, 1195, 1586, 1978, 2369)
R <- c(389, 786, 1180, 1571, 1963, 2354, 2745)
cen <- (L + R) / 2

# Four random example CDAs per score (0-6)
set.seed(42)
n_per <- 4
thumbs <- lapply(0:6, function(sc) {
  files <- list.files(here("data", "cropped_images", sc), full.names = TRUE, pattern = "\\.tif$")
  lapply(sample(files, n_per), function(f) as.raster(readTIFF(f)))
})

# Layout in pixel units (bottom to top): key panels, "Scoring Key" title, grid of boxed examples, score labels.
# Boxes are centred on the key panels but a little narrower, leaving clear gaps between columns.
box_hw <- 160
pad <- 16
tgap <- 12
side <- 2 * box_hw - 2 * pad
title_band <- 150
lab_band <- 150
box_h <- n_per * side + (n_per - 1) * tgap + 2 * pad
g0 <- key_h + title_band # grid (box) bottom
g1 <- g0 + box_h # grid (box) top
Htot <- g1 + lab_band

boxes <- data.frame(xmin = cen - box_hw, xmax = cen + box_hw, ymin = g0, ymax = g1)

thumb_layers <- list()
for (j in 1:7) {
  for (i in seq_len(n_per)) {
    ytop <- g1 - pad - (i - 1) * (side + tgap)
    thumb_layers <- c(
      thumb_layers,
      annotation_raster(thumbs[[j]][[i]],
        xmin = cen[j] - side / 2, xmax = cen[j] + side / 2,
        ymin = ytop - side, ymax = ytop, interpolate = TRUE
      )
    )
  }
}

p <- ggplot() +
  annotation_raster(key_raster, xmin = 0, xmax = W, ymin = 0, ymax = key_h, interpolate = TRUE) +
  annotate("text", x = W / 2, y = key_h + title_band / 2, label = "Scoring Key", size = 7) +
  thumb_layers +
  geom_rect(
    data = boxes, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
    fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = cen, y = g1 + lab_band / 2, label = 0:6, size = 8) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(0, W), ylim = c(0, Htot), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void()

ggsave(here("analyses", "02_score_distributions", "thesis_plots", "cdaexamples.png"),
  p,
  width = W / 300, height = Htot / 300, dpi = 300, device = ragg::agg_png, bg = "white"
)
knitr::include_graphics(here("analyses", "02_score_distributions", "thesis_plots", "cdaexamples.png"))
```

**What this shows:**

- Four randomly selected example CDAs for each median score (0-6, upper panel), aligned above the published scoring key (lower panel).
- Within a score class there is substantial variation (lighting, veins, damage, black background regions), while distant classes are clearly distinguishable and adjacent classes can be hard to tell apart.

### 2.2 Score counts (all scores and median scores)

```{r fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6
# 2.2
all_counts <- score_data_valid %>%
  count(Score, name = "Count") %>%
  mutate(Score = factor(Score, levels = 0:6))

median_counts <- score_data %>%
  count(Median_Score, name = "Count") %>%
  mutate(Median_Score = factor(as.integer(Median_Score), levels = 0:6))

# Largest-remainder rounding so displayed percentages sum to exactly 100.0
pct_sum_100 <- function(counts, digits = 1) {
  scaled <- counts / sum(counts) * 100 * 10^digits
  floor_vals <- floor(scaled)
  deficit <- round(100 * 10^digits) - sum(floor_vals)
  top_up <- order(-(scaled - floor_vals))[seq_len(deficit)]
  floor_vals[top_up] <- floor_vals[top_up] + 1
  floor_vals / 10^digits
}

all_counts <- all_counts %>% mutate(Pct = pct_sum_100(Count))
median_counts <- median_counts %>% mutate(Pct = pct_sum_100(Count))

cat("All-score counts:\n")
print(all_counts)
cat("\nMedian score counts:\n")
print(median_counts)

most_common_median <- median_counts[which.max(median_counts$Count), ]
least_common_median <- median_counts[which.min(median_counts$Count), ]
cat(sprintf(
  "\nMost common median score class:  %s (n = %d, %.1f%%)\n",
  most_common_median$Median_Score, most_common_median$Count, most_common_median$Pct
))
cat(sprintf(
  "Least common median score class: %s (n = %d, %.1f%%)\n",
  least_common_median$Median_Score, least_common_median$Count, least_common_median$Pct
))

p_all <- ggplot(all_counts, aes(x = Score, y = Count, fill = Score)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), vjust = -0.5, size = 5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sev_pal, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = "Severity Score", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11)
  )

p_median <- ggplot(median_counts, aes(x = Median_Score, y = Count, fill = Median_Score)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), vjust = -0.5, size = 5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sev_pal, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = "Median Severity Score", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11)
  )

p <- p_all + p_median
p
save_plot(p, "score_counts.png", width = 12, height = 6, dir = "thesis_plots")
```

**What this shows:**

- The left panel shows each individual score collected across all raters. The right panel counts the median score of each CDA, which will be used as the ground-truth label.
- 0 is by far the most common score in both views.
- Intermediate scores (3-4) are more numerous than higher (5-6) or lower (1-2)

### 2.3 Dotplot of all scores, faceted by median score

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=14}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 14
# 2.3
score_data_raw <- score_data %>%
  mutate(across(c(Score1, Score2, Score3), ~ replace(., . == "[]", NA_character_)))

set.seed(123)
score_data_random <- score_data_raw[sample(nrow(score_data_raw)), ]
score_data_random$row_index <- seq_len(nrow(score_data_random))

desired_order <- c("6", "5", "4", "3", "2", "1", "0")
score_data_random$Median_Score <- factor(as.integer(score_data_random$Median_Score), levels = desired_order)

p <- ggplot(score_data_random, aes(x = row_index, y = as.numeric(Score))) +
  geom_point(aes(y = as.numeric(Score1)), color = "black", alpha = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(y = as.numeric(Score2)), color = "black", alpha = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(y = as.numeric(Score3)), color = "black", alpha = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 6)) +
  labs(x = "Annotation Index", y = "Severity Score") +
  theme_minimal() +
  facet_wrap(~Median_Score, ncol = 2) +
  theme(
    strip.text   = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text    = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title   = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 11)
  )
p
save_plot(p, "all_scores.png", 10, 14)
```

**What this shows:**

- This plot shows the spread of scores collected for each median score group in a slightly different format, allowing patterns of disagreement to be more clearly visualised for smaller, non-0 classes.
- This plot shows the spread of scores collected for each cell death area. The X axis is grouped by median score.
- Raters often provide disagreeing scores for the same image, and these disagreeing scores are most commonly adjacent to the median score, although a smaller number may be much further away.
- The median score 0 group appears to have fewer disagreeing scores.

## 3. Score frequencies by rater

### 3.1 Score percentage by rater (heatmap)

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
# 3.1
score_freq <- score_data_valid %>%
  group_by(Scorer, Score) %>%
  summarise(Count = n(), .groups = "drop")

score_pct <- score_freq %>%
  group_by(Scorer) %>%
  mutate(proportion = Count / sum(Count))

scorer_totals <- score_freq %>%
  group_by(Scorer) %>%
  summarise(Total = sum(Count), .groups = "drop")

scorer_labels <- setNames(
  paste0(scorer_totals$Scorer, "\n(n=", scorer_totals$Total, ")"),
  as.character(scorer_totals$Scorer)
)

p <- ggplot(score_pct, aes(x = Scorer, y = factor(Score), fill = proportion)) +
  geom_tile(color = "black") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", proportion * 100)), color = "black", size = 4.5, vjust = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(name = "Percentage\n(within Rater)", low = "white", high = "firebrick") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = scorer_labels) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "Rater", y = "Severity Score") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
p
save_plot(p, "score_pct.png", width = 10, height = 7)
```

**What this shows:**

- This plot shows distribution of scores collected by each rater as a percentage. It removes the replaces the count variable, making comparisons between raters easier.
- It shows that the number of 0s collected by rater 5 is indeed lower than any other rater, and the number of 6s higher than any other rater.
- It shows patterns that could be attributed to certain scoring behaviours. For example, rater 10 collected many more 1s than any other rater, but very few 0s. Rater 10 may have a different approach to differentiating between these scores than other raters. In contrast, rater 1 collected almost no 1s or 2s, but many 0s.
- Some raters (1, 5, 7) scored far fewer cell death areas than others.

## 4. Missing scores

### 4.1 Missing score frequency by rater and median score (bubble)

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=12}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 12
# 4.1
score_data_nas <- score_data_long %>%
  filter(Score == "[]" | is.na(Score))

if (nrow(score_data_nas) > 0) {
  nas_freq <- score_data_nas %>%
    group_by(Scorer, Median_Score) %>%
    summarise(Count = n(), .groups = "drop")

  p <- ggplot(nas_freq, aes(x = Scorer, y = Median_Score)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = Count, color = factor(Median_Score)), stat = "identity") +
    geom_text(aes(label = Count), vjust = 4, color = "black", size = 5) +
    scale_size_continuous(name = "Frequency", range = c(1.19, 25)) +
    scale_color_manual(name = "Median Severity\nScore", values = sev_pal) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:6) +
    labs(x = "Rater", y = "Median Severity Score") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 11)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.6, 6.2))
  print(p)
  save_plot(p, "missing_scores.png", width = 10, height = 12)
} else {
  message("No missing scores in canonical data.")
}
```

**What this shows:**

- This plot shows the number of scores that were missed by each rater. A missed score means that a rater did not record an annotation for a cell death area which was scored by two other raters. The median score on this plot is the agreed score of the remaining two raters who did record an annotation.
- The majority of missed scores were on class 0 cell death areas.
- Rater 10 missed far more scores than others - 36 compared to the next nearest of 23.

---

## 5. Discussion

### 5.1 Score distributions

- The score distributions collected reflect experimental design and biological outcomes. Some experiments have quite binary outcomes (0 or 6) whilst others have more balanced phenotypes, showing a range of intermediate scores.
- A score of 0 is common because of both experimental (intentional negative control included in all experiments) and biological (no expression or no immune response) outcomes.

### 5.2 Missing scores

- Missed scores represent intentional choices, not accidental omissions.
- The annotation tool includes a skip button which the annotators were instructed use for cell death areas that were highly unclear (e.g. leaf folding), damaged, or overlapping with adjacent cell death areas. Different interpretations of these descriptions may account for the variable skip counts.
- Score 0 was the most common score collected, so it being the most commonly missed makes sense. Damaged leaves (often caused by the agroinfiltration syringe puncturing the leaf) also often appeared as score 0.

## 6. Additional visualisations

### 6.1 Dotplot of all scores, sorted by median score

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 8
# 6.1
score_data_sorted <- score_data_raw %>%
  arrange(Median_Score) %>%
  mutate(row_index = row_number())

boundary_df <- score_data_sorted %>%
  group_by(Median_Score) %>%
  summarize(boundary = max(row_index)) %>%
  mutate(boundary = boundary - 0.5)

group_labels <- score_data_sorted %>%
  group_by(Median_Score) %>%
  summarize(center = mean(row_index), .groups = "drop")

p <- ggplot(score_data_sorted, aes(x = row_index, y = Score)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = as.numeric(Score1)), alpha = 0.1, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(y = as.numeric(Score2)), alpha = 0.1, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(y = as.numeric(Score3)), alpha = 0.1, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_vline(data = boundary_df, aes(xintercept = boundary), color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text(
    data = group_labels,
    aes(x = center, y = 6.45, label = as.integer(Median_Score)),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, fontface = "bold", size = 5
  ) +
  annotate("text",
    x = 0, y = 6.45, label = "Median Severity Score:",
    hjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = 5
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:6, limits = c(0, 6.6)) +
  labs(x = "Annotation Index", y = "Severity Score") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text    = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title   = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 11)
  )
p
save_plot(p, "dotplot_scores_sorted_by_median.png", 14, 8)
```
